title: The coefficient change $a_X$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of condensed rings, i.e. a morphism of ring
objects of condensed abelian groups ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and let $X$ be a scheme. The
*coefficient change* on $X$ is

$$
a_X:=p_X^*a\colon\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda'_X=p_X^*\Lambda',
$$

the image of $a$ under the inverse image $p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. It is a
morphism of ring objects of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ between the coefficient rings of
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients].

proof.text: For the given scheme $X$, use the functor on ring objects of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], whose object assignment is $\Lambda\mapsto p_X^*\Lambda=\Lambda_X$ and whose ring structures are transported along $p_X^*$. Apply this functor to the given ring-object morphism $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$. Its underlying morphism is $p_X^*a$, with source $\Lambda_X$ and target $\Lambda'_X$, and it is a ring-object morphism because it is a morphism in that functor's target category. Define $a_X$ to be this morphism. This is precisely the displayed definition.

lean.statement:
noncomputable abbrev coefficientMap (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    condensedRingObj Λ X ⟶ condensedRingObj Λ' X
lean.note: Exact existing construction in the published upstream pro-etale framework, read in the shared side overlay and confirmed with scompile.py --source. In section CoefficientMap, Λ and Λ' are condensed abelian sheaves, with MonObj structures and IsMonHom a when regarded as ring objects. The abbreviation is (upperStarFromPoint X).map a; Functor.map.instIsMonHom supplies its ring-homomorphism structure. Equivalently it is the underlying arrow of (upperStarFromPoint X).mapMon.map (Mon.Hom.mk a), between coefficientRing X (Mon.mk Λ) and coefficientRing X (Mon.mk Λ'). No commutativity is assumed. The recorded point pullback sfbPullbackFromPoint is an abbreviation of this same upperStarFromPoint. The branch label denotes the published WeilConjectures source root; no duplicate module is introduced.
